step1.description: Cleaning of existing surface (asphalt, concrete or bitumen). No earthwork, no milling. The surface simply needs to be flat and stable. Marking anchor locations.

step2.description: URBAQUAI modules arrive on site ready to install. Placement by slings (1,800 kg capacity). Central module M 1.18: ~1,400 kg, lateral modules: ~700 kg.

step3.description: Module alignment using factory-mounted spacing studs. Fixing with Ø12 mm anchors at 15 cm depth into existing surface. Inter-module assembly.

step4.description: Installation of wheelchair access ramps (concrete D-009a or galvanized steel with automatic height adjustment and tamper-proof hardware). Tactile guidance strip verification. Platform immediately usable.

contenu: Law No. 2005-102 of February 11, 2005 establishes the principle of generalized accessibility throughout the travel chain.
It requires that all public transport stops be made accessible to people with reduced mobility.
Accessibility Master Plans – Programmed Accessibility Agendas (SDA-Ad'AP) set compliance deadlines for each organizing authority.
conformite: Standardized platform height (18-21 cm) for step-free access

contenu: The CEREMA guide "Bus and coach stops accessible to all" (2018) is the technical reference for project owners and designers.
It details geometric requirements, docking aids, and complementary facilities for each configuration type.
URBAQUAI was designed in strict compliance with all recommendations of this guide.
conformite: Platform geometry compliant with CEREMA templates

contenu: Standard NF P 98-352 defines mechanical strength, durability and sizing requirements for prefabricated concrete curbs.
It specifies flexural strength, abrasion, freeze/thaw and chemical attack (de-icing salts) tests.
URBAQUAI high-performance concrete exceeds the standard's minimum thresholds on every criterion.
